chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Mis'mam, Abu Sayyar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Sayyar, indeed the state of the Muhrim (one in Ihram) is restrictive. If he kisses his wife while not desiring and he is Muhrim, then upon him is the blood of a sheep. And if he kisses his wife while desiring and he ejaculates, then upon him is the blood of a camel, and he seeks forgiveness from Allah. And whoever touches his wife while Muhrim with desire, then upon him is the blood of a sheep. And whoever looks at his wife with desire and ejaculates, then upon him is the blood of a camel. And if he touches his wife or lies close to her without desire, then there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِم: The person in the state of Ihram, restricted from certain acts during Hajj/Umrah
key_terms.دَمُ شَاة: The blood of a sheep (a type of expiation offering)
key_terms.لاَزَمَهَا: He lay close to her / cohabited

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a Muhrim who kisses or touches his wife during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* details the graduated financial expiations (kaffarah) for a Muhrim engaging in intimacy with his wife, distinguishing between acts performed with or without sexual desire (shahwah) and whether ejaculation occurred. It establishes a jurisprudential hierarchy where mere touching without desire incurs no penalty, while kissing with desire without ejaculation requires a sheep, and acts leading to ejaculation demand a camel, reflecting the principle of proportional liability in Shia fiqh.
